tei:titleStmt.tei:title: תְּחִנָה לְשַׁבָּת מְבָרְכִים רֹאשׁ חוֺדֶשׁ מְנַחֵם אָב
Tkhine for Shabbat Mevorkhim Rosh Ḥodesh Menaḥem Av (1877 and 1910)

tei:div.tei:head: Tkhine for Shabbat Mevorkhim Rosh Ḥodesh Menaḥem Av (1877 and 1910)

tei:lg.tei:l: Father in Heaven, see how we, your nation Yisra’el, stand and beg you to comfort us like a Father. Forgive our sins for which we were driven out of our land and sent far away from our soil. In this month of Menaḥem Av your Holy Temple was burned. Woe unto us, and woe unto our soul, when the light of our eyes, that is the Holy Temple, was taken from us. When it stood it caused our sins to be forgiven. In this month there was a joyous holy day to which there was no comparison. But now, this month is only full of tears and cries, when we remember the grandeur that was taken from us.

Dear God, hear the weeping of Tsiyon and accept the anguished cries of Yerushalayim, for she wails with a bitter heart. Just as you burned her with fire, so rebuild her with fire. As it says, “I will be to her (Yerushalayim) a wall of fire encircling her.” Praised are you, the Comforter of Tsiyon and the Builder of Yerushalayim. Amen.

tei:note.tei:p: In the blessing of the new month, Av is referred to as מנחם אב (Menaḥem Av, “Av of Comfort”), a reference to the consoling legend that the Moshiaḥ will be born on Tishah b’Av and the day turned into the most joyous day of the year.
A reference to the festival of Tu b’Av. Cf. Mishna Taanit 4:8, Babylonian Talmud, Ta’anit 30b-31a
